html-creator.name: Nordlys Trails · travel site with pictures
html-creator.description: A cinematic one-page site that places seven bundled pictures: zooming hero, trip cards, a lightbox and numbers that count up.
html-creator.prompt: Design a cinematic one-page site for the fictional small-group hiking company Nordlys Trails, set in an invented northern region called Varnmark; name no real country or place. Night-sky palette: deep navy, glacier white, an aurora-green accent, large elegant type. The page never scrolls sideways. 1) A full-height hero with overflow hidden: hero-aurora-ridge.svg sits on its own absolutely positioned layer behind the text (object-fit: cover) and only that layer zooms slowly (scale 1 to 1.12 over 20 s, alternating). A soft gradient darkens just the bottom third, so the picture stays bright. Centred headline 'Walk where the sky moves', one line of copy, and a button that scrolls to the trips. 2) A sticky translucent navigation bar. 3) Six trip cards in a responsive grid, one per remaining picture: Fjord Sunrise (4 days, easy, EUR 890), Forest Hut Loop (3 days, easy, EUR 640), Glacier Lake Traverse (6 days, hard, EUR 1,480), Lighthouse Coast (5 days, moderate, EUR 1,120), Plateau Cabin Nights (4 days, moderate, EUR 980), Midnight Sun Kayak (3 days, easy, EUR 760). The picture zooms gently when the card is hovered. 4) Clicking a card opens a lightbox with the picture fitted inside the window (max-width 90vw, max-height 80vh), the trip name, previous and next buttons; the arrow keys and Escape work too. 5) A band of three numbers that count up when it scrolls into view: 6 routes, 12 guests per group, 1,480 km of trail. 6) Sections fade and slide in as they scroll into view (IntersectionObserver). 7) A short footer with hello@nordlystrails.example. 8) A small badge fixed in the bottom-right corner of the window, always visible, that reads 'FICTIONAL DEMO -- no real bookings'. Prices are illustrative demo values. Keep the code compact.
html-creator.next_step: Press Generate, then Full screen. The seven pictures are fictional drawings shipped with the app; the model places them by name and they are embedded into the page.

html-creator.name: Neon Breakout · a playable game
html-creator.description: A complete brick-breaker written in one go: mouse, touch and keyboard, particles, levels and a score.
html-creator.prompt: Build a complete, playable brick-breaker game in one page, titled NEON BREAKOUT with the small subtitle 'written on this laptop, no cloud', on a dark synthwave background with a faint grid. Canvas: a fixed drawing size of 800 by 600 that never changes; scale it only with CSS (width: min(94vw, 120vh), height auto) and convert pointer positions to canvas coordinates with getBoundingClientRect. Bricks: six rows of ten, one neon colour per row; each brick is 71 wide and 22 high, 8 apart, the first one 8 from the left edge and the first row 60 from the top. The paddle follows 'pointermove' (mouse and touch alike), and moves while the left or right arrow key is held. When the ball hits the paddle its horizontal speed depends on where it lands: (hit position minus paddle centre) divided by half the paddle width, times the ball speed. The ball speeds up slightly with every brick, leaves a short glowing trail, and each broken brick throws a small burst of particles. Score, lives (3) and level are shown above the canvas. Keep one variable `state` with exactly four values: 'ready' (the game starts here: everything drawn, ball resting on the paddle, the hint 'Click or press Space to start'), 'playing', 'paused' (draw 'Paused'), and 'over' (draw a panel on the canvas with 'Game over', the score and 'Click or press Space to play again'). One 'pointerdown' listener on the canvas (not click plus touchstart) and the Space key both call exactly this function: function onAction() { if (state === 'over') { resetGame(); state = 'ready'; } else if (state === 'ready') { state = 'playing'; } else if (state === 'playing') { state = 'paused'; } else { state = 'playing'; } } -- resetGame() restores score 0, 3 lives, level 1 and a fresh wall of bricks, and is called from nowhere else. When the ball falls below the paddle: take one life; with no lives left set state to 'over', otherwise put the ball back on the paddle and set state to 'ready' (score, lives and bricks are kept). When every brick is gone: raise the level, speed the ball up, build a new wall, put the ball back on the paddle and set state to 'ready' (score and lives are kept). One requestAnimationFrame loop updates and draws. Canvas calls and CSS only: no images, no sound, no external files. Keep the code compact.
html-creator.next_step: Press Generate, then Full screen and click the game once so it takes the keyboard. Everything is drawn by the generated code.

html-creator.name: Three engines · this laptop's AI, animated
html-creator.description: An animated infographic of this machine's CPU, GPU and NPU, using the figures the demo unit itself reports.
html-creator.prompt: Create a full-window, animated hardware board titled 'Three engines, one laptop' about the AI hardware of this demo machine, a Dell XPS 14 with an Intel Core Ultra X7 358H. Use exactly these figures and invent no others: CPU -- 16 cores (4 performance, 8 efficient, 4 low-power efficient). Integrated GPU, Arc B390 -- 122.9 INT8 TOPS, and about 36 GB of shared memory it can address. NPU -- 50.4 INT8 TOPS. Memory -- 64 GB, shared by all three. Dark theme (#070b14) with Intel blue (#0068b5) and cyan (#3fd0ff) accents, large numbers readable from a distance. Use this layout on the body: display grid; grid-template-columns repeat(3, 1fr); grid-template-rows auto 1fr 1fr auto; gap 16px; height 100vh; padding 16px; box-sizing border-box; overflow hidden -- so the board fills the window with no page scroll. The header and the last tile span all three columns; rows 1 and 2 each hold three tiles side by side. Behind everything, a slow particle field on a fixed full-window <canvas> (pointer-events none). Header: the title on the left, 'Figures reported by this demo unit, not datasheet values' on the right. Row 1, three large chip tiles with the ids cpu, gpu and npu: 'CPU' with the number 16 and the unit 'cores'; 'GPU - Arc B390' with 122.9 and the unit 'INT8 TOPS'; 'NPU' with 50.4 and the unit 'INT8 TOPS'. Each number is very large and counts up when the page loads, using exactly this helper so that it ends on the exact figure: function countUp(el, target, decimals) { const start = performance.now(); function step(now) { const t = Math.min((now - start) / 1500, 1); el.textContent = (target * t).toFixed(decimals); if (t < 1) requestAnimationFrame(step); } requestAnimationFrame(step); } -- called for 16 with 0 decimals, 122.9 with 1 and 50.4 with 1. Each tile has one short line saying what the chip is best at. Row 2, three tiles. 'AI throughput': two horizontal bars, each on a track as wide as the tile, that grow from zero when the page loads, GPU to 100 percent of its track labelled 122.9 TOPS and NPU to 41 percent labelled 50.4 TOPS. 'Sixteen cores': 16 squares in two rows of eight, coloured by type (4 performance, 8 efficient, 4 low-power efficient) with a legend, lighting up one after another. 'Shared memory': one bar standing for 64 GB, with a fill whose CSS width is exactly 56.25% (36 of the 64 GB) labelled '36 GB addressable by the GPU', and '64 GB total' at the bar's end. Row 3, one wide tile, 'Which engine for which job?': three buttons -- Speech, Vision, Language. Clicking one adds the class 'glow' (a bright cyan outline and shadow) to the matching chip tile, found with document.getElementById -- Speech: 'npu'. Vision: 'gpu'. Language: both 'gpu' and 'npu' -- removes it from the others, and shows a one-line reason next to the buttons. No external files. Keep the code compact.
html-creator.next_step: Press Generate, then Full screen. The figures come from the prompt, which states what this demo unit reports; the model is told not to add any.

html-creator.name: Kestrel · live operations wall
html-creator.description: A wall display that moves by itself: ticking KPIs, a scrolling chart, an event feed, pause and speed controls.
html-creator.prompt: Create a full-window operations wall for the fictional delivery company Kestrel Parcel, driven by simulated data generated in the page. Header: 'Kestrel Parcel -- operations wall' on the left, a 'SIMULATED DEMO DATA' badge, and a 24-hour clock that ticks every second on the right. Dark theme (#0b1220), teal (#2dd4bf) and amber (#f59e0b) accents, large numbers readable from a distance. The layout is a CSS grid that fills the window exactly (100vh, no page scroll on a wide screen). 1) Four KPI tiles updated on every tick: 'Parcels today' starts at 1,240 and only ever goes up (add 0 to 4); 'On-time rate' drifts by up to 0.2 between 90.0 and 99.0 percent; 'Vans on the road' changes by at most 1 between 18 and 32; 'Average delivery' changes by at most 1 between 22 and 35 minutes. Each tile shows an arrow for the direction of its last change, green when that is good and red when it is bad. 2) 'Parcels per minute': a line chart on a <canvas> sized to its tile, starting with 40 points already filled; on every tick a new point is added on the right and the oldest dropped, so the line scrolls left. Soft gradient fill under the line, a few faint horizontal grid lines. 3) 'Parcel status': a doughnut in inline SVG (viewBox 0 0 42 42) made of three <circle> elements with r=15.915, fill none and stroke-width 6, so the circumference is 100: each segment has stroke-dasharray 'share 100-share' and stroke-dashoffset 25 minus the sum of the shares before it. Delivered (teal), in transit (blue) and delayed (amber) start at 62, 30 and 8 percent, shift by a point or two every few ticks while always summing to 100, and animate with a CSS transition; the legend shows each percentage. 4) 'Latest events': a feed of six rows; every second tick a new invented event (for example 'Van 12 left depot North', with the clock time) is added at the top with a brief highlight and the oldest is removed. 5) A Pause/Resume button and a speed selector (1x, 2x, 5x) that restart the single setInterval with a period of 1000 ms divided by the speed. No external files. Keep the code compact.
html-creator.next_step: Press Generate, then Full screen. Every number is made up by the page itself each second; nothing is fetched.
